title: A Ember for the Thorn Anew
premise: Felix Galloway, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, has survived by hiding her gift and guiding smugglers through the Thornfell mountains. When the crown's witch-hunters burn the border village that sheltered her, she flees with a ragged found family: a disgraced royal cartographer, a mute child who hears swords too, and an ex-hunter whose loyalty she cannot trust. Their only escape lies through the Door of Aember, a passage into the drowned kingdom of Thornfell that exists only in oath-memory — and only Felix can speak it open. In the end, Felix must choose between sealing the door forever to save her companions or speaking her true name aloud, sacrificing her identity so the child can inherit the gift and the lost country can be remembered rather than resurrected.
about_author: Xanthe Hartwell is the pen name of a former mountain guide who traded trail maps for story maps after a winter snowed in with nothing but a battered notebook. They write fantasy about borders — of countries, bodies, and hearts — from a cabin full of rescued hounds.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: Felix Galloway guides a contraband caravan through the Thornfell passes, using her forbidden swordspeech only once, secretly, to turn aside a rockslide. A hunter's badge glints on one passenger she was paid not to look at. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: wary competence shadowed by the loneliness of a gift that must stay silent.

chapters.title: Ash on the Border Road
chapters.summary: Felix returns to Hollowmere village to find it burned by the crown's new hunt for the gifted. She rescues Wren, a mute girl clutching a singing sword shard, and discovers the ex-hunter Aldric among the survivors, stripped of his badge. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: grief hardening into resolve; the first sparks of found family.

chapters.title: A Cartographer of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Disgraced mapmaker Isolde Vane offers passage in exchange for protection, claiming she has charted the Door of Aember — the way into vanished Thornfell. The hunters' drakes pass overhead as they flee. POV: Isolde. Emotional beat: guilt over the maps she sold the crown, and tentative trust offered anyway.

chapters.title: What the Sword Remembers
chapters.summary: In a ruined watchtower, Felix teaches Wren the first words of swordspeech, breaking her own vow of silence. Aldric confesses he helped draft the hunt's lists — including Felix's name. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: tenderness toward Wren colliding with fury and reluctant forgiveness toward Aldric.

chapters.title: The Hunt Takes the High Pass
chapters.summary: Ambushed at the high pass, the group splits; Isolde is captured while buying their escape. Felix speaks a blade awake before witnesses, confirming the rumors of the last swordspeaker. POV: Aldric. Emotional beat: shame transformed into commitment as he chooses her side openly.

chapters.title: Bargains Below the Snowline
chapters.summary: To learn where Isolde is held, Felix bargains with the smuggler-queen Maren Ost, paying with her most guarded secret: her true name, which anchors the Door of Aember. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: the terror of identity as currency, and the cost of love already outpacing duty.

chapters.title: The Prison of Quiet Bells
chapters.summary: They infiltrate the mountain prison where the gifted are 'hushed.' They free Isolde but find rows of silenced children, and Wren refuses to leave them behind. POV: Isolde. Emotional beat: horror at complicity, then fierce maternal defiance as the family grows beyond plan or safety.

chapters.title: Where the Map Ends
chapters.summary: Pursued by the hunt's commander, Serah Dain — once Felix's sworn sister — they reach the Door of Aember as winter seals the pass. Serah offers Felix pardon if she surrenders the children. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: old love against present duty, and the door opening only to a spoken name.

chapters.title: The Speaking of Names
chapters.summary: At the threshold, Felix realizes the Door demands a true name freely given — hers. Instead she teaches Wren to speak it, passing the gift and the memory of Thornfell to the child, unmaking her own oath-bound identity. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: sacrifice as inheritance; grief and wonder braided together.

chapters.title: An Ember Carried Forward
chapters.summary: Nameless but free, Felix walks out of the mountains with her family as the Door closes behind them, Thornfell preserved in Wren's keeping rather than consumed by war. Serah lets them go, carrying the ember of doubt home. POV: Felix. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — identity rebuilt not by blood or oath, but by those who walk beside you.
